title: BGP Labs: filter advertised prefixes
license_review: BGP Labs uses MIT. FRR uses GPL-2.0-or-later; its source release and COPYING are linked and pinned separately from the image digest.
check_meaning: The checkset includes session, advertised customer-prefix and withheld loopback-prefix controls on both external routers.
evidence_label: Checked on this PC (live BGP observations)
availability_reason: Reviewed FRR control-plane adaptation for local Linux x86-64 Docker.

integration.stop: netlab down destroys topology compute; collect configuration before stopping.
integration.support_files: Keep repository defaults.yml and plugins; copying only topology.yml is insufficient.
integration.version_requirement: This selected topology requires netlab 26.06 or newer (the single-session task declares 25.12.03). Exact netlab/containerlab/FRR image pins and VM lifecycle measurements are pending.

instructions: This is a control-plane adaptation of the pinned BGP Labs exercise using FRR 8.4.1. Run local-lab show RUN to see router addresses, AS numbers and exact local vtysh connection commands. Configure rtr, use show bgp ipv4 unicast summary and show bgp ipv4 unicast to investigate, then run local-lab check RUN. Save changes with write memory. Stop/resume retains the configuration; reset creates a new attempt. It does not configure kernel forwarding or run netlab.

measurements.download_scope: Pinned compressed OCI layers/config plus selected sources and licenses; shared cache may reduce downloads. Not a wire-traffic measurement.
measurements.scope: Host filesystem sampled every 50 ms; unrelated activity may contribute. Memory is summed cgroup peaks including measurement execs. Images were absent at each start. Memory peaks were read after the final resume/check; cgroup restarts reset earlier epochs, so this is not a full-cycle memory maximum. Warm startup excludes route convergence and checking. Reviewed resource limits were inspected in every container.

objective: Advertise the customer prefix while withholding the router loopback from both external peers.
